release: The report now says what the site is BUILT on. A post-deployment check that only proves the new site is a faithful copy has not proved it is a production site — "is this really WordPress behind Cloudflare, or did the staging build go to production" is a question every crawl already held the evidence for, in the HTML it fetched and the headers that came back, and never asked. A new "Built on" panel names the CMS (WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, Drupal, Joomla, Ghost, HubSpot), the framework (Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Gatsby, Angular, Vue, React), e-commerce (WooCommerce, Shopify, Magento, BigCommerce), and the server and CDN read from response headers (nginx, Apache, LiteSpeed, IIS, Caddy; Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify, CloudFront, Fastly, Akamai). Every signature carries a page count, because a CMS seen on 1 of 40 pages is a part-migrated site and not the same fact as one seen on all 40. Detection is offline and deterministic — no extra requests, no third-party service. IT REPORTS SIGNATURES, NEVER CERTAINTY: a generator tag can be removed and a header can be spoofed or stripped by a proxy, so an empty list means no signature was seen, not that the technology is absent, and that caveat travels ON the data rather than living in the renderer so no surface can show the lists without it. Post-Deployment Check gets all of it for free, because it already runs a full audit of the target as production validation — which is also where Largest Contentful Paint and Cumulative Layout Shift already fire.
